A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core framework, experiments and appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of all 28 pages of v2 and 30 pages of v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original SAE experiments, a 1,000-question human study, LLaVA steering results, and appendix analyses of reconstruction, concept hierarchies and uniqueness.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations on additional encoders and a quantitative steering comparison against Difference-in-Means.

M1.justification: The central proposed scoring procedure changes: Equation 9 and Figure 2 replace division by N(N−1) with division by summed pair relevance. This substantively changes MS outputs for given activations. SAE architectures, reconstruction objectives and activation-clamping steering remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or the earlier formula was erroneous.

E1.justification: v3 broadens steering coverage from the existing poem, scientific-title and image-description examples to ten generation prompts, including mathematical problems, dialogue, rap and newspaper writing (Appendix B). ImageNet and the appendix iNaturalist task are retained. Additional encoders change model coverage rather than the represented image datasets.

E2.justification: Section 4.3 and new Table 2 introduce Difference-in-Means as an evaluated competitor for concept insertion and suppression. This supplies a competitive steering comparison absent from v2, whose quantitative steering comparison was against unsteered outputs. Existing BatchTopK, Matryoshka and No SAE comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The reported MS normalization changes in Equation 9. v3 also introduces a GPT-4.1-mini evaluation using 100 SAE neurons and ten insertion prompts, with concept-control and preservation criteria, and adds AIMv2/WebSSL model configurations. Table A1 revises interval sample counts while retaining the stated 1,000-question, 71-annotator study; these changes do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 2 quantitatively examines steering side effects through prompt adherence and preservation of unrelated concepts, extending v2's qualitative specificity examples. Existing width/sparsity analyses, iNaturalist hierarchies, reconstruction analysis and concept-uniqueness checks remain substantively unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting for neuron scores and image–text steering similarities. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Revised user-study counts and percentages do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds encoder results in Table 1b and steering results in Table 2: joint success is 42.4% versus 35.8% for insertion and 52.5% versus 33.3% for suppression against DiffMean, although insertion alone is 48.7% versus 53.1%. Reported human alignment changes from 79.0% to 82.8%; Figure 4 and Table A1 are revised. Table 1a, Tables A2–A11 and the old steering-similarity table retain their values. The metric revision precludes interpreting the alignment update as a straightforward same-setting gain.

T1.justification: Equation 9 substantively revises the formal definition of the paper's principal metric to a relevance-normalized weighted average. Summing unordered instead of ordered pairs is equivalent by symmetry, but replacing pair-count normalization with relevance normalization changes the mathematical quantity. No new theorem or proof accompanies this revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: neuron-level MS evaluation aligned with human judgment, improved monosemanticity through sparse/wider SAE representations, and concept insertion or suppression through vision-encoder interventions. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the added encoder results as evidence of applicability across training objectives and emphasizes steering selectivity. Its limitations now explain that a golden-retriever neuron may induce generic dog outputs and that some feature detectors have no clear steering effect. Limited MLLM fine-grained understanding and encoder–language misalignment are offered as possible explanations.

D1.justification: v3 specifies additional encoder variants and token extraction, names the GPT-4.1-mini judge, and lists ten generation prompts in Appendix B. Its abstract and main text report benchmark-data availability where v2 promised release, although Appendix D retains future-tense wording. The new comparison still lacks detailed DiffMean construction and judge instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning activation steering, feature-selection limitations, AIMv2/WebSSL and broader VLM applications and reliability, including Arditi et al. and Arad et al. The related-work discussion expands, but its three-part organization and principal positioning around neuron-level SAE evaluation and vision-based steering remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and several captions receive localized rewriting. Section 4.3 places quantitative evaluation before qualitative examples, and the publication header changes to NeurIPS 2025. The overall section structure and most methodological and appendix prose are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a two-panel display, a new steering Table 2 is added, and the former Table 2 becomes Table 3. Figure 2 revises the score diagram and Figure 4 updates the plotted alignment results. Captions, table sizing and float placement change, while the qualitative examples and appendix displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens steering validation with a competitive baseline and explicit checks of prompt and unrelated-content preservation, addressing a gap in v2's qualitative and CLIP-similarity evidence. The normalized MS definition and concrete steering limitations improve precision. The gain remains limited by incomplete baseline/judge specifications and the unexplained relationship between the revised formula and retained MS tables; the higher reported alignment percentage alone does not establish improved validity.
